summary: A 59-foot Aermotor tower on Encino Point, first erected on the Kaibab National Forest and re-erected here in 1950.

facts.design: 59-ft Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with a 7x7 ft steel cab
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Santa Fe National Forest (Coyote Ranger District)

events.note: First erected at Skinner Ridge on the Kaibab NF; the 2020 review gives 1929 or 1933
Santa Fe NF moved the abandoned Skinner Ridge tower to a Santa Fe warehouse
Cerro Valdez L-4 cabin and log cabin moved to the Encino site in November 1949
Encino site constructed in July 1950 as it presently exists; tower erected there
Regular staffing ended and the lookout closed; the history gives 1983 or 1984
Encino complex found not eligible in the 1988 thematic National Register review

evidence.supports: 59-ft Aermotor MC-39 steel tower with 7x7 steel cab
evidence.quote: Encino lookout is an Aermotor MC-39 steel tower 59 feet high, and a 7X7 foot steel cab.

evidence.supports: first erected at Skinner Ridge, Kaibab NF, 1929 or 1933; still standing 1941
evidence.quote: The lookout was originally erected in 1929 or 1933 at Skinner Ridge on the Kaibab National Forest and was still standing there in 1941 according to Barbara Zinn’s document.

evidence.supports: forest moved the abandoned tower to a Santa Fe warehouse in 1948
evidence.quote: In 1948, the Forest moved the abandoned Skinner Ridge Lookout tower from the Kaibab National Forest to the Santa Fe Warehouse.

evidence.supports: meant for Barillas; erected at Encino Point after 1949 decision
evidence.quote: but when the Regional Office abandoned Barillas in 1949, the Skinner Ridge tower was erected at Encino Point instead.

evidence.supports: Cerro Valdez L-4 cabin and log cabin moved to Encino in 1949
evidence.quote: The Cerro Valdez L-4 Lookout and its log cabin were moved to the Encino site in the fall of 1949.

evidence.supports: cabins skidded to Encino Point in November 1949
evidence.quote: In November 1949, Orbie Bridge of Regina used a bulldozer to skid both Cerro Valdez cabins to the new site at Encino Point.

evidence.supports: site constructed July 1950 as it presently exists
evidence.quote: The Encino site was constructed in July 1950 as it presently exists.

evidence.supports: Manuelita took over as primary lookout in the mid-1970s
evidence.quote: Manuelita took over as the primary Encino lookout when her husband took other Forest work in the mid-1970s.

evidence.supports: staffed until mid-1980s with Norman Montoya as relief
evidence.quote: She staffed it until the mid-1980s, with Norman Montoya as her relief.

evidence.supports: regular staffing ended 1983 or 1984 when lookout was closed
evidence.quote: This continued until 1983 or 1984, when Encino Lookout was closed.

evidence.supports: Montoya went up by day in fire season; little manning
evidence.quote: After that time, Norman Montoya went up during the day and came back down in the afternoons during fire season, but there was not much manning of the Encino Lookout anymore.

evidence.supports: 2020: only lookout on Coyote RD and currently staffed
evidence.quote: Encino is currently the only lookout on the Coyote Ranger District and is currently staffed.

evidence.supports: 1988 thematic review found complex not eligible
evidence.quote: was found not eligible due to move of the L-4 and log cabins being moved from the Cerro Valdez location, and the Lookout was not yet 50 years old on site.

evidence.supports: complex now 70 years old; should be re-evaluated
evidence.quote: Now that Encino lookout and the complex is 70 years old, it should be re-evaluated

evidence.supports: register lists the Lincoln National Forest
Coyote Ranger District heading within Santa Fe National Forest
evidence.quote: Lookouts Santa Fe National Forest – Coyote Ranger District:

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 1950 date is for the Encino site as it now stands. The tower itself was first erected at Skinner Ridge in 1929 or 1933, per the 2020 review.
The register lists the Lincoln National Forest, but its own cooperator line and the 2020 review name the Coyote Ranger District, which the Santa Fe NF history places on the Santa Fe National Forest.

sources.title: Fire Lookout History of the Santa Fe National Forest
sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service, Santa Fe National Forest (April 2017), hosted at npshistory.com

notes_for_editor: Staffing conflict: the Santa Fe history's appendix says regular manning ended in 1983 or 1984 when the lookout closed, while the 2020 review says it is currently staffed. No source read explains when staffing resumed. Access level not set: no visitor, rental or trail-access information in the sources. Forest name conflict: register says Lincoln NF, other sources say Santa Fe NF. The history's history of the 1929/1933 first erection is not settled; the story reports both dates.
